from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Two blocks collide on a frictionless surface.",
            "Tiny block m approaches massive block M.",
            "M is one hundred to the n times m.",
            "They bounce off a wall to calculate pi."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Counter-Intuitive Hook", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        block_m = Square(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).set_height(0.5)
        block_M = Square(color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).set_height(1.5)
        wall = Line(start=UP*2, end=DOWN*2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(block_m, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(block_M, 'C5')
        self.place_at_grid(wall, 'C6')
        self.play(FadeIn(block_m), FadeIn(block_M), FadeIn(wall))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        label_momentum = Text("Momentum", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label_momentum, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(label_momentum))
        self.play(block_m.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#0000FF")
        vec_m = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color="#0000FF", buff=0)
        vec_M = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT*0.3, color="#0000FF", buff=0)
        vec_m.next_to(block_m, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        vec_M.next_to(block_M, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(vec_m), Create(vec_M))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        flash = Dot(color="#FFFF00", radius=0.3)
        flash.move_to(block_m.get_right())
        self.play(flash.animate.scale(3), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(flash))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Collisions to Phase Space", [
            "Track velocities as coordinates on phase space.",
            "The collision path traces a circular arc.",
            "Boundary walls force the path to reflect."
        ])
        
        # Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 6, 1], y_range=[-2, 6, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": "#808080"})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.add(axes)
        
        # State point
        state_point = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 2), color="#FF9900")
        
        # Trajectory (arc)
        arc = ArcBetweenPoints(axes.c2p(2, 2), axes.c2p(4, 0), angle=-TAU/4, color="#00FFFF")
        
        # Turning point
        turning_point = Dot(axes.c2p(4, 0), color="#FF0000")
        
        # Energy contours
        energy_contour = Circle(radius=axes.c2p(3, 0)[0]-axes.c2p(0, 0)[0], color="#CCCCCC")
        energy_contour.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), FadeIn(state_point))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF9900")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(arc))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(Create(turning_point))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(energy_contour))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Collisions relate to circular arc length.",
            "Arc length maps to the ratio pi.",
            "More mass yields more pi digits."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometric Connection", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a circle representing the energy shell. Color #FFFFFF.
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(circle, "A2", "D5")
        
        # Animate point moving along the circle. Color #FF0000.
        point = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        point.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(circle.point_from_proportion((self.time * 0.2) % 1)))
        
        self.play(Create(circle), FadeIn(point))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show normal vector to the circle. Color #00FF00.
        # Fade in arc showing collision angle. Color #0000FF.
        normal = Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.8, color="#00FF00")
        normal.add_updater(lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(circle.get_center(), circle.point_from_proportion((self.time * 0.2) % 1) + UP*0.5))
        
        arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI/4, color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(arc, "B4")
        
        self.play(Create(normal), Create(arc))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Demonstrate mapping collision to circle geometry. Color #FFFF00.
        label = Text("collisions ~ pi digits", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "E3")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Conservation Laws

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Hook
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: How can two simple blocks colliding on a frictionless surface calculate the digits of pi? Visualize the blocks: a small block (mass m) and a much larger block (Mass M = 100^n * m).
sections.example: A tiny hamster-sized block slides toward a massive elephant-sized block resting against a wall.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly review Elastic Collisions. Use a split-screen animation showing Conservation of Momentum (mv_i = mv_f + Mv_f) and Conservation of Kinetic Energy (1/2mv^2). Explain why these laws force the blocks to exchange velocity states.
sections.example: Visualize velocity as a vector arrow that shrinks or grows as energy is transferred during the 'bounce'.

sections.title: Mapping Collisions to Phase Space
sections.content: Introduce the 'Phase Space' diagram. Instead of tracking time, track the velocities of the two blocks as coordinates (x, y). The collision path traces a circular arc on a graph. The boundary conditions (wall and origin) force the trajectory to zig-zag.
sections.example: A laser pointer drawing a circular arc that hits a 'wall' and reflects, acting like a billiard ball in a restricted angle.

sections.title: The Geometric Connection
sections.content: Explain that the total number of collisions is proportional to the arc length of the circular segment. As M becomes infinitely larger (100^n), the arc segment length relates directly to the ratio of the circumference to the diameter (pi).
sections.example: Show an animation where for M=100m, there are 31 collisions; for M=10,000m, there are 314 collisions.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition Check
sections.content: Summarize how discrete physical events (collisions) map onto continuous geometric constants. Emphasize that pi isn't just about circles, but about the periodic nature of symmetry and conservation.
sections.example: A final visual of the digit sequence 3-1-4-1-5 appearing on a scoreboard as the blocks bounce, finalizing the link between mechanics and pure math.
